heard: An orange dwarf star is hurtling straight toward our solar system. Sitting 62.3 light years away in serpents, precision data from the Gaia spacecraft reveals a shocking path. Astronomers tracked Gliese 710, heading toward us at roughly 14.5 kilometers per second. In about 1.29 million years, it will plow directly into our solar system's OOIT cloud. At a closest approach of 10,520 astronomical units, it becomes the brightest object in our night sky besides the sun, moon, and Venus. While major planets remain safe, its immense gravity will dislodge millions of icy comets. This gravitational disturbance triggers 10 naked-eye comets per year, proving an orange dwarf star is is hurtling straight toward our solar system.
